newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy ends down on profit-taking after new high.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy ends down on profit-taking after new high.

text.p: CBOT soybeans traded higher most of the session but the market was pushed to lower closes by a wave of profit-taking after the July contract made new highs, traders and analysts said.
"We're still in a very tight stocks situation," said Jason Roose, analyst with U.S. Commodities in West Des Moines, Iowa. "This is still a bullish market, but we just saw late profit-taking."
The market fell soon after July surpassed its old contract high of $8.92-3/4 a bushel as commodity funds, commission houses and local traders exited long positions, traders said.
Strength in the market had initially stemmed from ideas that soybean prices needed to rise more to ration and demand.
The U.S. Department of Agriculture put weekly net export sales at a healthy 383,300 tonnes. That figure fell within trade expectations of 350,000 to 450,000 tonnes.

Some traders said expecations for a falling weekly soybean crush weighed on soybean prices. Most in the trade expect the crush to fall below last week's crush of 25.644 million bushel, with estimates ranging from 24.1 to 24.9 million.
Soybeans settled one cent a bushel higher to ten cents per bushel lower, with July down 10 cents at $8.77 per bushel.
